t: Monthly SLA reporting and service credits
h:
Service operations and facilities · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Monthly SLA reporting and service credits

Bernardo · Vendor Performance Analyst

An outsourced services provider manages 18 contracts, each with 6 to 12 service level indicators and its own penalty formulas.

When it runs
First business day of each month at 9 a.m., after the period's tickets are closed in the ticketing system; rerun for the specific contract when the customer formally disputes
What it delivers in production
One measurement report per contract on the second business day with each indicator calculated and the proposed penalty with the clause that supports it and the calculation breakdown, for the manager's approval before billing.
Who decides
Calculates and proposes penalties; the manager approves
Effort
Calibrate on 3 accepted months; 2 months reviewing everything

# Indicators per contract and calendar

## Contract C-07 (on-site technical support, sites S1 São Paulo and S2 Campinas)
Coverage: business days, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., at both sites. Outside that, the clock stops.

| Indicator | Formula | Target | Penalty bands | Clause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 P1 first response | median, in coverage minutes, from opened to first_response of the P1 tickets | up to 30 min | above target: 1% | 9.1 |
| I2 P2 resolution within 8 h | P2 tickets resolved within 8 coverage hours divided by the P2 tickets of the month | 90% or more | up to 10 points below: 2%; more than 10 points: 4% | 9.2.a and 9.2.b |
| I3 Reopening | reopenings divided by the month's tickets that are not reopenings | up to 10% | above target: 1% | 9.3 |

Exclusion (clause 8.3): a 'waiting on customer' pause leaves the time only with contact_logged = yes.
No C-07 indicator is tied to a termination clause.

## Holiday calendar (October and November 2026)
| Date | Holiday | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 12 | Our Lady of Aparecida | national |
| Nov 2 | All Souls' Day | national |
| Nov 20 | Black Consciousness Day | national |

## Rules with no leeway
- Time only within coverage hours, without weekends and holidays. E.g.: C-0707, opened Friday Oct 9 at 5 p.m. and resolved Tuesday Oct 13 at 11 a.m., adds 2 h + 4 h = 6 h, within 8 h.
- A pause with contact_logged = no or empty is provider time. E.g.: C-0709 stays at 10 h (out), not 7 h; C-0710 stays at 14 h.
- A reopening stays out of I1 and I2 and counts only in I3. E.g.: C-0716 (reopens C-0706); I2 has 11 P2 tickets, I3 = 1 of 15 = 6.67%.
- No rounding before comparing. E.g.: I1 with responses of 20, 30, 31 and 45 min has a median of 30.5 min, above 30, off target.
- Penalty and approvers. E.g.: I1 1% + I2 2% (81.82%, 8.18 points below) = 3% of R$ 120,000 = R$ 3,600. The contract manager always approves; above 2% the operations manager joins; I2 off target for the 3rd month in a row (Aug, Sep and Oct) goes to operations leadership and legal. All of them apply.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent applies only the interpretation recorded in the indicator table; when a clause allows two readings, it calculates both and shows the difference, without choosing the one that favors the provider. A 'waiting on customer' pause is only removed from the time when there is a contact record on the ticket, because a pause with no contact is the most frequently lost dispute. A proposed penalty does not become a discount on the invoice without the manager's approval, and no indicator reaches the customer before then. The calculation breakdown is always generated, including for contracts with no penalty.

Common mistakes

  • Excluding all time in a 'waiting on customer' pause; without a contact record, the customer disputes and wins.
  • Applying headquarters' coverage hours and holidays to a site in another municipality; the municipal holiday changes the indicator in tight contracts.
  • Rounding availability to one decimal place and declaring 99.5% when the measured figure was 99.47%; the customer's audit will find it.
  • Measuring by average when the contract says percentile; the annex formula overrides the system's habit.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Business days to close the measurement for the 18 contractsfrom 6 to 1 to 2estimate based on the described routine
Measurement disputes per quarterfrom 2 to 0 to 1, with a calculation breakdown available in every oneestimate based on the described routine
Match with historical measurements accepted by the customer95% of indicatorsestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Service level measurement, contract C-11 (on-site technical support, 3 sites), period August 2026, 412 tickets. Draft for manager approval. Indicator | Summary formula | Target | Measured | Status | Penalty
P1 response time | median of 1st response within coverage hours 7 a.m.-7 p.m. | 30 min | 27 min | within | 0
P2 resolution time | 90th percentile, coverage hours, 'waiting on customer' pauses excluded (clause 8.3) | 8 h | 9 h 20 | outside | 2% of the monthly amount, band 1 (clause 12.1.a)
Time clock system availability | minutes unavailable outside an approved window | 99.5% | 99.47% | outside | 1% of the monthly amount, band 1 (clause 12.2)
Reopening within 72 h | tickets reopened / closed | 3% | 2.1% | within | 0 || Backlog older than 10 days | tickets open at month end | 5 | 3 | within | 0
PROPOSED PENALTY: 3% of the monthly amount (R$ 4,140 on R$ 138,000). Approver: contract manager (band up to 2%) and operations manager (above 2%).
NOTES: municipal holiday on 15/08 at site 2 excluded from coverage (clause 5.2); 6 P2 tickets with a 'waiting on customer' pause and no contact record, treated as provider time, breakdown in the P2 tab; availability 0.03 point from the target, check the 21/08 window that was not formally approved.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You are the service level meter of an outsourced services provider. You propose; the contract manager approves; you do not bill or send anything to the customer.

CONTEXT
contract_indicators.md, attached, gives per contract the formula, target, coverage, exclusions, penalty bands, clause and holidays per location. The recorded interpretation prevails.

INPUT
month_tickets.csv with ticket, contract, site, priority, opened, first_response, resolved, reopened_from, pause_reason, pause_start, pause_end, contact_logged. maintenance_windows.csv with contract, start, end, approved_by. contract_values.csv with contract, monthly_value. prior_measurements.csv with contract, indicator, month, measured. Without the contact_logged column, treat every pause as provider time and flag it in the header.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Convert times to the coverage hours of the contract and site, without weekends and local holidays.
2. Exclude a 'waiting on customer' pause only with contact_logged = yes; empty or no, it is provider time and goes into the breakdown.
3. Compute each indicator with the table formula and compare it with the target.
4. Off target: penalty band and clause; add up the contract's penalty in percent and in R$.
5. Point out indicators within 5% of the target and windows without formal approval that affect the result.
6. Compare with the 3 prior months and flag an indicator off target for the third month in a row.
7. Write the calculation breakdown per indicator with the tickets counted and excluded.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not round before comparing with the target. Do not choose between ambiguous interpretations; present both. A reopening is not a new ticket: it stays out of the times and counts only in reopening. Send nothing to the customer.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with contract, period, tickets and the sentence 'Draft for manager approval'. Table: Indicator | Short formula | Target | Measured | Status | Penalty with clause. PROPOSED PENALTY line with percent, R$ and all approvers. NOTES block with exclusions, pauses treated as provider time and points of attention.

ESCALATION
All bands that apply hold. The contract manager always approves. Penalty above 2% of the monthly value: add the operations manager. Above 5%, target missed for the third month in a row or indicator tied to a termination clause: add operations leadership and legal, before talking to the customer.
